reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Phase 03's code reading is correct — the code at line 328 does access cell_proofs[i * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB + j] without bounds validation. However, this finding is DISPUTED per bug bounty scope rules. The 01e property (file: 01e_PARTIAL_W3B4_1771748827.json, lines 699-715) explicitly marks this property as 'bug_bounty_scope: conditional' because it involves the Engine API. The property has 'attacker_controlled: false' and 'entry_points: [EngineAPI, Consensus]', indicating it requires a compromised or buggy local EL to trigger. Per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json, the Engine API is semi-trusted (authenticated via JWT, co-located with CL), and while vulnerabilities requiring a compromised local EL may be in scope conditionally, the bug bounty program out-of-scope section states vulnerabilities requiring publicly exposed APIs are excluded. More critically, nimbus_beacon_node.nim:2045 shows the only reachable call path validates blobsEl.len == blob_kzg_commitments.len BEFORE calling assemble_data_column_sidecars, ensuring blob count matches commitments. The REST API path (rest_beacon_api.nim:1108) decodes kzg_proofs from RestPublishedSignedBlockContents, which would undergo standard deserialization validation. While the function itself lacks defensive bounds checking, all observed call paths provide data from semi-trusted sources with structural guarantees.
